description: Language-neutral conformance vectors for Conformity 1.0/1.1/1.2 records, partial presentations, packages, statuses and summaries. Generated from real issued artifacts by scripts/generate-conformity-conformance-suite.ts; keys are synthetic test keys.

comparison.absent: A member absent from expected must be absent from the report, except members the suite does not compare.

profiles.neutral: expected: a verifier with no product-specific extension handlers or source policy.
profiles.prooftask: profiles.prooftask overrides expected for the ProofTask reference verifier, which also replays ProofTask workflow events and names retired ProofTask formats.

notCovered: Anchoring evidence (evidence/, package standard 1.2): RFC 3161 tokens, OpenTimestamps and Bitcoin headers, and the REVOKED-key pre-exposure rule that depends on them.
Party-signature anchors and ProofTask participant keys.

cases.description: Conformity 1.0 package: both parties agreed, one delivery, explicit second-party ACCEPT; full disclosure.
Conformity 1.1 package with signed limitations; every limitation code is reported.
Conformity 1.2 package: a third-party technical evaluation (V, EVALUATE) by an actor delegated with scope VERIFY, then the explicit second-party ACCEPT.
Valid record whose latest decision is REQUEST_CHANGES: verified, closure NOT_COMPLETE.
A namespaced (URI) history event after the decision: interpretation becomes INDETERMINATE, closure NOT_COMPLETE.
An unknown noncritical extension is covered by the signature and ignored.
An extra file not reached from the signed commitments: UNCOMMITTED_FILE, listed in ignoredFiles, verdict unchanged.
Partial presentation: the same issuer-signed JWT with one criterion judgment disclosed.
Partial presentation with no disclosures: only always-visible claims.
Conformity 1.1 partial presentation disclosing the criteria; limitations stay visible and are reported.
Conformity 1.2 partial presentation disclosing the criteria; the delegated evaluation stays visible as signed structure.
Every disclosure but presented as a bare SD-JWT (no package): still a partial presentation, closure not established.
Signing key RETIRED but the signature time lies inside [validFrom, validUntil): still valid.
Signing key validUntil equals the record issuedAt: the window is half-open, so the record signature is outside it.
Record key validFrom equals issuedAt (inclusive start), events signed by key-2: valid.
JEP events are checked at their own recorded time: key validFrom after the first event makes the event signature untimely.
ACTIVE status does not override an explicit validUntil before issuance.
Conformity 1.0 record under a REVOKED key: INVALID (1.0 keeps the 1.0 report).
Conformity 1.1 record under a REVOKED key with validUntil and no anchoring evidence: INDETERMINATE.
REVOKED key that states no validUntil: INDETERMINATE with HISTORICAL_KEY_VALIDITY_UNKNOWN.
A partial presentation carries no evidence, so under a REVOKED key it is always INDETERMINATE.
Only the key that signed the JEP events is REVOKED: the record is still INDETERMINATE.
Conformity 1.0: JEP events under a REVOKED key make the record INVALID.
The relying party trusts no key for this issuer.
The trusted issuer has keys, but none with the JWT kid.
Two trusted keys share the kid: ambiguous, no key is selected.
The trusted key-1 is a different Ed25519 key.
The trusted key-1 is a P-256 key.
A disclosure value changed (and the package file digest updated): the disclosure is no longer referenced.
Partial presentation with a modified disclosure.
The same disclosure presented twice.
A full package whose record.sd-jwt omits one disclosure.
The JWT payload changed without a new signature.
A compact SD-JWT without the trailing tilde.
Issuer-signed JWT whose typ is not sd-jwt.
Protected header with a member other than alg, kid and typ.
Conformity JWTs use alg EdDSA; the RFC 9864 name Ed25519 is not accepted here.
_sd_alg other than sha-256.
Signed disclosureCount differs from the number of commitments.
JWT iat differs from issuance.issuedAt.
JWT iss that is not a URL at all: not an HTTPS issuer origin.
JWT iss and identity.issuer differ.
A disclosed value itself contains an _sd commitment (nested disclosures are forbidden).
A disclosure whose salt has fewer than 128 bits.
A disclosure whose salt is not base64url: an invalid disclosure, not a transport error.
An _sd entry that is not a base64url SHA-256 digest.
A critical extension the verifier has no handler for.
An unknown critical extension inside a concealed criterion still fails a partial presentation (criticalManifest is visible).
The reserved org.humanjudgment.party-signature extension is not implemented and is rejected.
ACCEPT decision with a NOT_MET verdict: ACCEPTANCE_NOT_CONFORM (registered by the 1.2 catalog; earlier verifiers reported INVALID_CONFORMITY_INPUT).
A history kind that is neither registered nor a namespaced URI: UNKNOWN_UNNAMESPACED_EVENT (registered by the 1.2 catalog).
The delegated evaluation of the 1.2 case declared as Record 1.1: the 1.1 schema has no VERIFY scope, so the record keeps its own version and is rejected.
Record 1.2 technical evaluation whose actor is delegated with scope JUDGE: an evaluation needs scope VERIFY.
A 1.1 record whose limitations name a code first registered by the 1.2 catalog: each record version uses its own catalog.
Verdict MET mapped to outcome NONCONFORM.
A criterion changed after the specification digest was computed.
A decision note changed after the decision digest was computed.
current.state does not equal the state the history produces.
A history entry whose previousDigest does not name the previous event.
A 1.1 limitation code that is not in the reason catalog.
issuance.issuedAt without milliseconds (and iat to match): timestamps must be canonical UTC.
The signed criticalManifest omits a critical extension present in the reconstructed record.
A committed JEP event file replaced (digest updated in the carrier).
A committed attachment is absent.
A committed file presented with a different media type.
A carrier entry whose data does not match its own sha256.
Two carrier entries with the same path.
A carrier path with a parent-directory segment.
A committed carrier entry without its data member.
A package object with a member other than schema and files.
A presentation object that carries TSTO content next to the SD-JWT.
JEP events signed by a key other than the trusted key-1 they name.
TSTO subject is not the record result identifier.
TSTO target claims do not repeat the criteria.
TSTO integrity value does not match its content.
A JEP event binds a different object digest than the record object it covers.
The decision event says reject while the record says ACCEPT.
A JEP event `when` differs from the history recordedAt.
Status observed at checkedAt: FRESH, currentState CONFORM.
checkedAt equals expiresAt (half-open interval): STATUS_EXPIRED, current state unknown.
checkedAt one millisecond before observedAt.
The verifier expects a different head digest.
The presented state differs from the signed observation.
A Status checked without an expected head and clock.
A signed Status valid for more than 300 seconds.
A Status is a current statement: under a REVOKED key it is INVALID.
A Conformity Summary (VC 2.0, eddsa-jcs-2022).
The summary title changed after signing.
The proof verificationMethod names another did:web.
A JSON object that is no Conformity artifact.
A retired ProofTask format: a neutral verifier does not know it; the ProofTask profile names it RETIRED_FORMAT.
A package whose JSON repeats a member name (escaped spelling): strict parsing rejects it.

A record issued by the ProofTask runtime: request changes, corrected delivery, buyer confirmation. A neutral reader reports the product workflow events as JEP_AUXILIARY_NOT_INTERPRETED; the ProofTask profile replays them.
Partial presentation of the product record disclosing only the criterion judgments.
Product record with one committed workflow event rewritten (carrier digest updated).
